title: Silky Dark Chocolate Mousse
summary: A deep, airy dark chocolate mousse made the classic way with whipped egg whites and cream, set in the fridge.

ingredients.item: dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
ingredients.note: check the label for soya and milk
Use pasteurised eggs (see the egg safety tip).

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: put the chocolate, cocoa, espresso powder and hot water in the heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water and stir until smooth. Take off the heat. Gentle heat keeps the chocolate smooth; too much heat makes it grainy.

steps.title: Yolks
steps.text: whisk the yolks with 1 tbsp of the sugar and the salt for 30 s until a little paler, then stir in the warm chocolate until glossy. Leave 5 min until just warm. Yolks make the mousse rich and help it set.

steps.title: Whites
steps.text: whisk the whites to soft foam, add the rest of the sugar and whisk to soft peaks. Stir a quarter into the chocolate to loosen it, then fold in the rest until only faint streaks remain. Loosening first means the rest of the whites keep their air.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it in until the mousse is evenly brown. Soft peaks fold in easily; stiff cream makes the mousse grainy.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: spoon into the bowls, cover and chill at least 3 h, until set. Dust with cocoa to serve. As the chocolate firms, the mousse sets.

tips: A common mistake is folding into hot chocolate, which melts the whites; wait until it feels just warm.
Fold with a spatula in big, slow strokes and stop as soon as it looks even.
safety: Egg safety: Use pasteurised eggs. If you can't get them, use the 71 °C cooked-egg method (below), or skip this recipe if you are pregnant, very young, older or have a weak immune system.

71 °C cooked-egg method: whisk the yolks with 15 g of the sugar and 2 tbsp water in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until the mixture reaches 71 °C and thickens, about 4 min, then whisk it into the chocolate. Whisk the whites with the other 15 g sugar in a clean heatproof bowl over the same pan until they reach 71 °C, take off the heat and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks (a Swiss meringue), then fold in as described.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Do not freeze.
